channel.title: Reads
channel.description: Papers, research, books and projects surfaced from X

item.title: Learning optimal gaits and styles for terrain-adaptive quadruped locomotion
item.description:
Bellegarda and Ijspeert (EPFL) study how quadruped robots can learn to select and adapt gaits and locomotion styles across varied terrain, connecting bio-inspired gait theory with locomotion on legged robots.
Via @OWW: https://x.com/i/status/2124981549162512808

item.title: Trilobite-inspired record-setting lenses from NIST
item.description:
NIST researchers built record-setting lenses inspired by the eyes of prehistoric trilobites. It shows how biological optics can guide modern optical engineering.
Via @krichard121212: https://x.com/i/status/2124968511894167795

item.title: Multiple-Camera Tracking of Rigid Objects
item.description:
Robotics and computer-vision preprint by Martin and Horaud on tracking rigid objects with multiple cameras. Relevant to motion capture and robot perception.
Via @OWW: https://x.com/i/status/2124968446752383102

item.title: Principles of Power Electronics
item.description:
Kassakian's text on power electronics circuits, magnetics, semiconductor devices, dynamic modeling and control. It includes modern SiC and GaN devices, advanced converters and EMI.
Via @ebokify: https://x.com/i/status/2124959574725980596

item.title: Fundamentals of Power Electronics
item.description:
Erickson's third-edition text on switching converters, semiconductor devices, digital control, circuit modeling and stability analysis. A standard reference for power electronics design.
Via @ebokify: https://x.com/i/status/2124958505966670294

item.title: The Art of Electronics
item.description:
Horowitz's classic reference on electronic circuit design. It covers practical circuit measurements, oscilloscope examples, component data and design insight for students and practicing engineers.
Via @ebokify: https://x.com/i/status/2124958178609643958

item.title: GG-PA: composing single-molecule diffusion models with physics
item.description:
Blog post on a NeurIPS 2026 paper. Diffusion models trained only on single molecules are combined with physics at inference time to sample molecular complexes that none of the models saw in training.
Via @weizhouwangw: https://x.com/i/status/2124952818905645133

item.title: HydroCore Design: CAD-designed electrodes for water electrolysis
item.description:
Video on a project exploring CAD-designed electrode geometries with up to 148% more geometric surface area. The aim is to improve efficiency in hydrogen-producing water electrolysis.
Via @BuicanGeor10049: https://x.com/i/status/2124942924358033412

item.title: FORCE GPU physics engine benchmark
item.description:
Open-source, GPU-based physics engine with a browser benchmark. You can run it on any device and submit results through a prefilled GitHub issue to help profile performance across hardware.
Via @__rockbiter: https://x.com/i/status/2124937313021022629

item.title: Quantum physics can prove where you are
item.description:
Nature piece on research using quantum physics to verify a party's physical location. Of interest as an application of quantum effects to position verification and secure location-based protocols.
Via @x3int1: https://x.com/i/status/2124915969772716379

item.title: From Blueprint to Twin: A Scientometric and Systematic Review of Digital Twins in Infrastructure Operation and Maintenance
item.description:
Review of 263 papers on digital twins for infrastructure maintenance. It identifies five research themes, including BIM, predictive maintenance and structural health monitoring, and sets priorities such as physics-informed, uncertainty-aware models.
Via @arnaudmercier: https://x.com/i/status/2124912473698439388

item.title: If tiny primordial black holes exist, here's how we might find them
item.description:
MIT researchers propose that a primordial black hole captured by a sun-like star would make it explode, producing a blue/UV flash detectable by current telescopes. This offers a new observational test for primordial black holes.
Via @MIT: https://x.com/i/status/2124865881192661282

item.title: Dry, stretchy material for gel-free ultrasound imaging
item.description:
MIT mechanical engineers developed a dry, stretchable acoustic coupling material that could replace wet ultrasound gel. It may enable wearable ultrasound patches for continuous imaging at home or on the go.
Via @MIT: https://x.com/i/status/2123793284413763624
